audit_notes: Model: effective areal compliance of a tiled stiff skin on a soft bed under a rigid fouler base, written as a uniform-strain 1D problem whose surface displacement equals C*tau: C = 3*[t_bed/E_bed*(a/(a+l))^2 + t_skin/E_skin], where the load-spreading length l is limited to half a tile (0.25 mm) because tiles move independently (a continuous skin would spread over the shear-lag length 1.6 mm). Release stress sigma_c = sqrt(2w/C). Design: C = 3*(3.5e-9*0.907 + 1e-11) = 9.56e-9 m/Pa, sigma_c = 3.2 kPa. Baseline: uniform commercial topcoat (E = 1 MPa, 150 um, tile_size 0 = no spreading term): C = 4.5e-10 m/Pa, sigma_c = 14.9 kPa. Expected gain ~78 %, vs ~73 % for the continuous skin with its spreading correction. Caveats: the (a/(a+l))^2 correction is a simple area-scaling estimate, not a solved plate-on-foundation problem; a base straddling tile gaps loads the gap material in shear, which is soft and adds compliance (favourable). Structural: the 20 um gaps filled with 0.1 MPa bed material are weak spots under fender contact and may become preferred cyprid settlement grooves (cyprids favour grooves of their own size ~20-100 um? cyprids are ~500 um, so 20 um gaps are below their preferred scale, but diatoms and bacteria colonise such microgrooves). Hull strain up to 0.2 % is taken by the gaps: tile edge displacement 0.5 mm*0.002 = 1 um, gap strain 5 %, fine. Dimensionless: tile/base ratio 0.05, spreading factor 0.907, skin/bed modulus ratio 50. Simulation coefficient: effective compliance 9.56e-9 m/Pa (informational).
